title: Replication and Scientific Credibility
text:
Replication is often described as the cornerstone of scientific credibility. A single striking result, however dramatic, rarely convinces the wider community until other laboratories obtain the same outcome under comparable conditions. Yet replication is surprisingly rare, partly because journals tend to reward novelty over confirmation. As a consequence, many published findings have never been independently verified.

Some researchers have responded by launching large collaborative projects that repeat well-known experiments across dozens of sites. Their results have sometimes weakened claims that once seemed secure, which is uncomfortable but instructive. Critics, however, caution that failed replications do not always indicate error, since subtle differences in methods or samples can alter outcomes. The debate therefore concerns not only what is true but how evidence should be judged.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, why is replication surprisingly rare?
options: Journals tend to reward novelty over confirmation
Laboratories lack the funding to buy equipment
Scientists are forbidden from repeating experiments
Results are always too complicated to repeat

questions.text: According to the second paragraph, what have some researchers launched?
options: Large collaborative projects that repeat well-known experiments
A new journal that publishes only negative results
Private laboratories that sell test samples
Government rules limiting the size of research teams

questions.text: What is the author implying about claims that once seemed secure?
options: Some of them may not hold up when tested again
They were all deliberately falsified by researchers
They should be ignored by the scientific community
They were confirmed by every laboratory involved

questions.text: Why do critics think a failed replication may not prove the original result wrong?
options: Small differences in methods or samples can change outcomes
Failed replications are always caused by human error
Journals refuse to publish any replication studies
The original researchers never shared their data

vocabulary.definition: a fundamental part on which something else depends
the quality of being trusted and believed
the repetition of an experiment to check its results
the quality of being new and different

paragraph_translations: La replicación suele describirse como la piedra angular de la credibilidad científica. Un resultado llamativo, por dramático que sea, rara vez convence a la comunidad en general hasta que otros laboratorios obtienen el mismo resultado en condiciones comparables. Sin embargo, la replicación es sorprendentemente poco frecuente, en parte porque las revistas tienden a premiar la novedad frente a la confirmación. En consecuencia, muchos hallazgos publicados nunca han sido verificados de forma independiente.

Algunos investigadores han respondido lanzando grandes proyectos colaborativos que repiten experimentos conocidos en decenas de centros. Sus resultados han debilitado en ocasiones afirmaciones que antes parecían seguras, lo cual resulta incómodo pero instructivo. Los críticos, en cambio, advierten que las replicaciones fallidas no siempre indican un error, ya que pequeñas diferencias en los métodos o en las muestras pueden alterar los resultados. Por ello, el debate no trata solo de lo que es verdad, sino de cómo debe juzgarse la evidencia.
